liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Runs about nine minutes; around 4:40 Weir takes over the lead while Garcia lays out; At 5:20 Weir plays a descending three-chord transition lick, handing back to Garcia at six minutes, then a dreamy passage follows [13]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer rates the second-set jam from He's Gone onward as about as good as it gets [20]
- **Phil Zone** (1 review): The jam from Phil Zone into The Other One features Garcia's solo and Phil and Keith's re-emergence [21]
- **The Other One** (1 review): About five minutes into the jam, Keith plays circling lines reminiscent of Chick Corea [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Phil Zone**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-06-22.mtx.seamons.92375.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 35 songs; 244 min; rated 4.48/5 by 29 [1]
- **gd73-06-22.sbd.cribbs.17270.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 31 songs; 261 min; rated 4.63/5 by 27 [2]. Said about its sound: The matrix sound is nicely separated, making the instruments easy to follow; Matrix mix is excellent nearly throughout, apart from a few rough patches; Audience patches fill the gaps in the matrix very smoothly [13][15][16][18]
- **gd1973-06-22.sbd.clugston.5850.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 31 songs; 257 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Intermittent crackle noise runs through the first set and is believed to be on the master reels [3]
- **gd1973-06-22.sbd.cribbs.88347.flac16**: soundboard; 31 songs; 261 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd73-06-22.aud.weiner.gdADT19.16889.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 33 songs; 223 min; rated 4.56/5 by 34 [9]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is rich and full-bodied, with a few minor blemishes; Audience tape is extremely good and offers a welcome change of perspective from the many soundboards of this era; The soundboard cuts out mid-jam, so the audience tape is needed to hear it complete [12][14][20][22]

## Around the show

- A friend who attended the show ranked it among the best they had seen [11]
- This show follows 6/10, after the band had nearly two weeks off [18]
- The jam evokes both 1977 and 1969 playing; fans nicknamed it the Truckin up to BC Jam [21]
- Reviewer prefers the audience tape over the soundboard version because it has more energy [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-06-22.mtx.seamons.92375.sbeok.flac16**: taped by See Notes; transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: See Notes [1]. Also: Matrix transferred and mastered by Charlie Miller from master reel via PCM and DAT, Sound Devices 744T, to FLAC; Audience source (shnid 16889, Sony ECM mics to cassette) supplies the Other One section and the end of Casey Jones; A soundboard cassette lineage (shnid 85957) patches Bird Song, The Race Is On and I Know You Rider [1]
- **gd73-06-22.sbd.cribbs.17270.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [2]
- **gd1973-06-22.sbd.clugston.5850.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Sounbdoard Reel > PCM > DAT > CDR [3]. Also: Master audience reel DAT source patches The Other One, the end of Casey Jones and the Johnny B. Goode encore; Scott Clugston converted this fileset with EAC and SHN [3]
- **gd1973-06-22.sbd.cribbs.88347.flac16**: taped by Main source discs provided by Andy Lemieux.; transferred by encoding by Sean Cribbs.; source: MSR>PCM>DAT>CD>EAC>WAV [4]. Also: Fileset re-tracked, re-patched and encoded to FLAC in November 2007, using main source discs from Andy Lemieux; MSR chain covers Bertha to the cut in The Other One; a second MSR source completes the set; Patches in The Race Is On and I Know You Rider come from a cassette-based source (shnid 85957) [4]
- **gd73-06-22.aud.weiner.gdADT19.16889.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [9]
